A_target.statement:
Let $S \subseteq \R$ be [[Definition:Non-Empty Set|non-empty]] and [[Definition:Bounded Below Subset of Real Numbers|bounded below]].
Then $S$ has an [[Definition:Infimum of Subset of Real Numbers|infimum]].

B_source.statement:
Let $S \subseteq \R$ be [[Definition:Non-Empty Set|non-empty]] and [[Definition:Bounded Above Subset of Real Numbers|bounded above]].
Then $S$ has a [[Definition:Supremum of Subset of Real Numbers|supremum]].

object_map.reformulation: Reflect S through 0 (replace S by -S), which swaps upper and lower bounds and reverses the order.

validity_conditions: Negation x |-> -x is an order-reversing bijection of the reals, so bounds and their extremality swap exactly.
S bounded below iff -S bounded above, so the source hypothesis applies to -S.
proof_plan:
If $m \le x$ for all $x \in S$, then $-x \le -m$ for all $x \in S$.
So $-S$ is non-empty and bounded above.
By the [[Continuum Property|least upper bound property]], $\map \sup {-S}$ exists.

Let $\ell = -\map \sup {-S}$.
Then $\ell \le x$ for all $x \in S$, and if $m$ is any lower bound then $-m$ is an upper bound of $-S$, so $\map \sup {-S} \le -m$ and $m \le \ell$.
Hence $\ell = \inf S$.
{{qed}}
